result:
**Verdict: PASS.** I verified both findings assigned to me, found no regressions, and raised one new Low finding. The validator's `--reconcile` mode reads my record as "round 12 qa-verifier: PASS (current)".

I reviewed candidate `sha256:619d74ff…dfac`, frozen at commit `987ae02`. It recomputes to the same ID in a full disposable clone. HEAD differs from the freeze commit only by candidate-excluded metadata. During my run it moved to `163d0ca` when the runner auto-committed the domain reviewer's records; I didn't open those, and the ID didn't change. Since round 11, only `architecture.testkit.ts` and `architecture.test.ts` changed, so the fix is test-only.

**Findings verified (both now CLOSED_VERIFIED):**
- **F-DG1-132:** the new rule (`node:crypto` may only be imported by name) holds on Node 22 and Node 24:
  - **Project tests:** the project's own lint tests pass on both runtimes.
  - **My own probe (41/41 on both runtimes):** it flags 21 different ways of importing the whole crypto module, some of which the implementer's tests don't cover.
  - **Round-11 routes now flagged:** the 7 ways of reaching `setEngine` by listing the module's contents are all caught at the import.
  - **Runtime check:** a search of everything reachable from the 69 named exports never reaches `setEngine`.
  - **Real code is compliant:** the 5 module files that import crypto all use named imports.
- **F-DG1-133:** the lint file's header no longer calls the route "not closable statically" and no longer cites the two unrelated files. Ordinary object lookups like `request.cookies` are still allowed.

**Earlier fixes still hold (nothing regressed):**
- **F-DG1-214:** unit tests pass 315/315 on Node 22 and Node 24; the web project is 110/110 on both.
- **F-DG1-009:** integration tests pass 200/200 on three runs against a throwaway PostgreSQL, with no 57P01 errors.
- **F-DG1-210:** browser end-to-end tests pass 22/22 on both runtimes, in English and Arabic, with no accessibility violations. My own spec for this journey passes 2/2.
- **Database:** the API contract tests pass 9/9, including `getBrandingTokens`. Migrations 0001–0008 apply, and the audit table rejects every UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE.
- **Acceptance and static checks:** A12, A13, A14, A18 and A20 all pass. Build, typecheck, lint, the OpenAPI check (33 operations), the no-CDN check, formatting and colour contrast are all green.
- **Gate validators and requirements:** `--register DG1`, `--pipeline` and `--reconcile` pass. All 12 requirements are IMPLEMENTED, and none is missing an evidence file.

**BLOCKED:** one sub-case of the REQ-DLV-042 installer suite, "AC-1 (effect)", needs to download a package and my sandbox has no network. The other 13 cases pass. The installer code and its recorded 14/14 log haven't changed since round 11.

**New finding:**
- **F-DG1-216, Low, not mandatory (proposed ID):** decision D-055 in `docs/delivery/decisions.md` still says reaching `setEngine` by listing the module's contents is an accepted gap ("residual (a)"). The new rule now blocks that route. It's a one-line documentation fix, or it can be accepted as an observation. It doesn't block DG1.

The review record, its verifications and findings files, and a short narrative are in `docs/delivery/reviews/DG1/round-12/`. Logs and screenshots are in `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG1/qa/round-12/`, and the probe test is at `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG1/qa/tests/dg1-r12-rule5-probe.test.ts`. I've removed all the disposable clones.
